name: Xizha (West Scenic Area)
tagline: The larger, atmospheric side you stay overnight in
description: The bigger and more immersive of the two zones, Xizha is a maze of canals, stone bridges, waterside inns, workshops, and bars, and it is where the famous night illuminations shine. Many visitors stay overnight inside to enjoy the evening after day crowds thin.
pros: In-gate guesthouses let you enjoy quiet nights
Bars, workshops, and canal boats concentrated here
cons: Peak-season crowds and premium room prices

name: Dongzha (East Scenic Area)
tagline: The smaller, older, more workaday side
description: The original and more compact scenic zone, Dongzha showcases older streets, craft demonstrations like indigo dyeing and shadow puppetry, and a slightly more lived-in feel. It is usually visited by day and pairs naturally with Xizha via the shuttle bus.
pros: Good introduction to the town's heritage
cons: Less dramatic at night than Xizha

name: Modern Wuzhen Town (outside the gates)
tagline: The ordinary town beyond the ticketed zones
description: Outside the scenic gates lies the everyday town where locals live, with cheaper guesthouses, ordinary restaurants, shops, and bus links. It lacks the postcard canals but offers better value, authentic local meals, and a place to sleep without paying scenic-area premiums.
pros: Cheaper rooms and authentic local food
No scenic-area ticket needed to be here
cons: Limited English and few tourist comforts

name: Hangzhou / Tongxiang (regional base)
tagline: The real base for working and long stays
description: Tongxiang hosts the nearby high-speed rail station, while Hangzhou, about 30 to 40 minutes by train, is the sensible base for remote workers. Hangzhou offers coworking, apartments, coffee culture, and West Lake, letting you day-trip to Wuzhen while keeping a proper home base.
pros: Fast rail to Wuzhen, Shanghai, and beyond
Big-city amenities and a real expat scene
cons: Larger, busier, and pricier than Wuzhen
